finalText:
Migration is complete and verified.

**What I changed** — 36 call sites across 12 files that the earlier passes missed:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `admin/variantAdmin.js`, `repo/supplier.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `admin/macroAdmin.js`, `repo/sla.js` |

Each `db.query(sql, params)` became `db.execute({ sql, params })`, matching the formatting of the already-migrated modules (e.g. `packages/orders/src/repo/order.js`).

**Two things I deliberately left alone:**

- **`cache.query(...)` — 25 sites.** `packages/*/src/repo/*.js` call `cache.query('users:' + id)` on the cache handle from `lib/cache.js`. Same method name, unrelated API; a blind name-based sweep would have broken these. My rewrite anchored on the `db.` receiver, so they're untouched.
- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js` — 2 sites.** Vendored third-party code, replaced wholesale on upgrade, so local edits would be lost. It still calls `db.query`, which is fine while `lib/db.js` keeps the deprecated method. Worth flagging: when the driver's next major actually drops `query`, that adapter is the one thing that will break — it needs an upstream fix or a shim, not an edit in place.

**Verification:** `node verify.js` exits 0 — it confirms no `db.query` remains in `packages/`, every `db.execute` call carries both `sql:` and `params:`, the `cache.query` count is still 25, vendor is unmodified, and it then loads all 75 modules with `db.query` stubbed to throw and exercises each `get*`/`list*` function, asserting a real `execute` call with a string `sql` and array `params`. An independent grep confirms the only remaining `db.query` references repo-wide are in vendor and in the verifier's own message string.
